solution.what: Resumed existing local notes and IIIF scans; earlier Prague cipher transcription incomplete. Regenerated native-scale crops.
Inspected Breslau cipher at native scale; numeral order and digit grouping require renewed analysis. Earlier notes are unverified prior project work, not an independent decipherment.
Transcribed sixteen Prague recto insertions and May cipher into runs_draft.json; glyph and grouping uncertainties retained.
Tested 63 greedy one/two-digit prefix partitions. Unrestricted homophonic scoring collapsed to repeated letters; constrained swaps produced no coherent text. Testing point-delimited pairs next.
Swept 1566 retained forward/backward greedy prefix segmentations on the frozen initial draft; six pair variants and pointed-six null variants gave no coherent manuscript plaintext.
Expanded to 29 Prague insertions plus the two May spans; measured 834 and 77 draft digits. Rechecked f64 lower cipher against its repeated view on f65.
Imposed hypothetical mais...jamais, then ne/ni, in point-delimited pair parses of May. No coherent extension; all crib mappings rejected as unvalidated.
Constrained pair substitution solver recovered 538 of 538 synthetic plaintext letters. This verifies the restricted implementation, not the manuscript model. See control/result.tsv.
Read f63 reference to sending a copy of the cipher by one of two routes on 24 February to Sr Barquin (name provisional). Corrected par lune, previously misread as a place.
Located catalogue mirror for fr. 4695 no. 51, Labbe to Nevers, Prague 5 February 1577, Gallica btv1b90582923; plausible earlier correspondence, not inspected and not a demonstrated key enclosure.
New Gallica image/manifest requests failed by connection reset or timeout via Python, curl and browser; earlier-letter/enclosure trail remains externally blocked.
AngusRobinson (PR #20): guessed three similar figure strings as l'empereur / empereur, giving one- and two-figure units with homophones and 6 = word space.
AngusRobinson (PR #20): extended the key by decoding further passages; deciphered all 31 runs of nos. 30 and 37/38 (KEY_AND_DECRYPTION.txt).

Review: every token line decodes to the stated text (0 mismatches); PR figure streams agree with the independent 23 Sept draft in 897/914 figures (98.1%); five lines rechecked on the f65, f77 and f79 images; f77 53/35 is a copying slip, f79 reads retournoit.
Shuffle control, fr-1530-despatches LM: key -2.500 per char vs 1000 shuffled keys mean -8.137 (sd 0.469, best -6.738), z = 12.0.
Web search for a prior reading (Cryptiana, Nevers/l'Abbé 1577): none found.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 534 tokens, 28 types, fr-1530-despatches order 4: reading -2.269 per letter; random keys -6.422 (z 7.4); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -3.53 (mean -3.613, z 22.1); annealer on the real text -2.269. Verdict: pass.

Independent solution by George Lasry (with ChatGPT Astra 6 and Anthropic Opus 5.5), BnF cipher research, 10 Oct 2026: ciphertext-only, 526 of 533 elements identified plus the 43-element duplicate; his f75r reading (ne pleureroient) agrees with the PR #20 key; spot-checked on f75r 13 Oct 2026.

texts.label: Nos. 30 (Prague, 2 March 1577), 37 and 38 (Breslau, 2 May 1577): the cipher insertions, AngusRobinson's decipherment (PR #20)
texts.summary: Desiderio l'Abbé reports to Nevers from the imperial court. The March cipher runs concern Poland after Báthory's election (the nuncio of Mondovì, Zborowski, Danzig, "puisse prendre femme en hongrie", the Emperor and the "titre de roi", peace with the Turk; the Poles are divided and show Báthory a good face while their hearts are contrary); the May run follows Weber's resignation: "mais plusieurs ne pleureroient s'il n'y retournoit jamais".
texts.note: KEY_AND_DECRYPTION.txt is AngusRobinson's key, figure streams and plaintext per run (PR #20); reading_pr20.txt is this project's check (decode_pr20.py: figures, decode, PR plaintext). The surrounding clear text is outlined, provisionally, in prague_reading.md and breslau_reading.md. George Lasry's independent decipherment of 10 Oct 2026 (report slug labbe1577lasry) is not in the repository; only his f75r excerpt is quoted in NOTES.md.

reading_review.note: SOLUTION.txt read through: the cipher in these letters is short insertions (1-12 words) inside clear French, and every insertion decodes to clean French with no hole (two blotted figures restored from context, one writer's slip, trouer). The insertions are complete; what is missing is the surrounding clear text, which is outlined, not transcribed (prague_reading.md, breslau_reading.md), so whole sentences need the clear text from the images. Audit grade C overturned for the decipherment itself.
